name: tax identification number (TIN)
note: Austria's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: Austria's TIN is issued by the local tax office of the taxpayer's residence when the taxpayer asks it for a service, only to individuals liable to tax, and changes if the residence moves; 9 digits (written 99-999/9999). The sheet gives no other name for it. Read as given on application, to residents. No check rule, age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Austria: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: The Local Tax Offices issue TINs to the taxpayers having their residence in the area of competence of these Offices, when they ask the local office for a service. This means that a TIN can change when a taxpayer changes residence. ... TINs are only issued to individuals who are liable to tax. ... 99-999/9999 9 digits
